title: Sluice & Highbanker Tuning: Flow, Angle, and the Gravel You Feed
scope: Practical editorial guide synthesized from original recovery research, government field guidance and manufacturer instructions. No Gold Trails recovery trial or universal optimum is claimed.

sources.title: Fine Gold Recovery of Selected Sluicebox Configurations
sources.publisher: G. W. Poling and J. F. Hamilton; University of British Columbia / Canada–Yukon research program, undated report
sources.location: Printed pp. 60–61, sections 5.4–5.5; discussion of clay and suspended solids
sources.supports: Slope, water and feed interact; riffle-specific scour patterns; similar scour across tested slopes; muddy appearance alone is not a recovery measurement.
sources.limits: Specific test geometry, feed and gold fractions; short trials do not establish performance of modern hobby mats or long-duration clay loading.

sources.title: Gold Losses at Klondike Placer Mines — Gold Recovery Project (Phase 1)
sources.publisher: Government of Yukon; original placer recovery project report
sources.location: Government report abstract: sampling design and difficult feed conditions
sources.supports: Representative discharge sampling, nugget effect, clay/fines and heavy-mineral challenges; recovered plus lost gold mass is required for recovery estimation.
sources.limits: Commercial placer sampling is more rigorous than a recreational pan check; historical operating rates are not prescribed here.

sources.title: Placer Gold Recovery Methods — Special Publication 87
sources.publisher: Michael Silva; California Division of Mines and Geology, 1986
sources.supports: Gravity concentration, riffled sluice operation, site-specific recovery, classification and testing.
sources.limits: Historical equipment guidance; its traditional sluice velocity recommendations are not universal targets for modern mats.

sources.title: Dream Mat FAQ
sources.supports: 7–12 degree family-level starting range dependent on flow and material; cell exchange; clay liberation.
sources.limits: Manufacturer guidance, not independent recovery validation or an instruction for every mat design.

sources.title: High Banker Sluice Conversion Kit — instructions
sources.location: Setting up the sluice box, item 1
sources.verification: Official indexed PDF text inspected; direct PDF fetch returned HTTP 403
sources.supports: Approximately 10 degrees initially for this kit, then adjust once water flow is established; avoid gravel buildup and excessive slope.
sources.limits: Specific conversion kit. Indexed text availability is recorded; direct PDF retrieval was blocked.

sources.title: Tuning Your Sluice — The Fear Factor
sources.location: Loading, capture-zone exchange and tailings testing
sources.supports: A slow, overloaded bed can lose gold; tailings gold alone does not diagnose excessive speed; particle shape affects behavior.
sources.limits: No general recovery percentage is adopted. Deliberately losing gold into an uncontrolled stream is not recommended.

sources.title: Tuning Your Gold Sluice — Part 2
sources.location: Slurry density / viscosity and feed-rate discussion
sources.supports: Solids loading and slurry character affect tuning; reducing feed relative to water is a possible adjustment.
sources.limits: Suspended silt/clay is not dissolved sediment; the source's loose terminology and proprietary superiority claims are not adopted.

sources.title: Prospecting Water Pumps — Some Basic Thoughts
sources.location: Lift, hose friction and delivered water
sources.supports: Pump label output differs from delivery through a lifted hose system.
sources.limits: No universal derating or advice to throttle an arbitrary pump is adopted; follow the pump's own instructions.

sources.title: Instructions for Using Your Sluice
sources.location: PDF pp. 1–2: intake/exhaust vents and fluidization
sources.supports: Fluidizing-vent systems require unobstructed intakes/exhausts and appropriate volume as well as speed.
sources.limits: A distinct recovery design; conventional riffle appearance rules cannot be applied blindly.

sources.title: 5.1 Stream Flow — Volunteer Stream Monitoring
sources.publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, archived guidance
sources.location: Discharge definition, cross-sectional area and surface-float method
sources.supports: Discharge differs from velocity; a float measures surface motion, which differs from depth-averaged flow.
sources.limits: Natural-stream correction factors are not validated for a shallow riffled sluice and are not used here.

editorialMethods: Small contained batches with all test discharge retained where feasible
Comparable prepared feed and A–B–A repeats
One control changed at a time, then coupled settings retested
No recovery percentage from a single tailings pan
Angle conversions use vertical drop divided by horizontal run
notClaimed: A universal best angle, GPH, depth or velocity
Visual confirmation of gold recovery from mat appearance
That muddy water alone proves poor recovery
